subject: Civic Education
competence: Broad curriculum competency standard in plain English
lesson: Explains the fact that the fulfillment of the expectations of a work place is a bounden duty of an employee: Courtroom / Citizen Grievance Tribunal: Competency Level 8.6.6
unique_learning_outcome: Explains the fact that the fulfillment of the expectations of a work place is a bounden duty of an employee.
Explains the need to be sensitive as a worker to the expectation of the work place.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: Imagine you are a new employee at a company. You have just received your first assignment. What are your expectations from your workplace? How do you plan to fulfill them? (5 minutes)

summary: What are the key takeaways from today's activity? How do you think fulfilling the expectations of a workplace is important for employees? (2 minutes)
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative feedback: Did the students demonstrate an understanding of the importance of fulfilling the expectations of a workplace? Did they show sensitivity to the expectations of the workplace?
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: In-class quiz: Can you recall the key points discussed in the courtroom scenario? (5 minutes)
selected_activity:
Activity: Courtroom / Citizen Grievance Tribunal: Competency Level 8.6.6
Approach: Students use courtroom / citizen grievance tribunal to explore 'Explains the fact that the fulfillment of the expectations of a work place is a bounden duty of an employee.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 40 students using 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
